tasks.instruction: Your friend has sent you an e-mail, and you have jotted down some notes. Use them to write your answer.

choices.title: E-mail to a friend
choices.prompt: Your friend Jamie is coming to visit you next weekend. Write an e-mail to Jamie. Answer the questions in the e-mail and use all four of your notes. Write about 100 words.
choices.input:
From: Jamie
Subject: Next weekend

Hi! I'm so excited about coming to see you next weekend. Is there anything special you would like to do on Saturday? I'd love to cook dinner for you one evening. What kind of food do you enjoy? Also, I'm arriving at the central station on Friday evening. How do I get to your apartment from there? Write soon!

Jamie

Your notes:
- Say how you feel about the visit.
- Suggest an idea for Saturday.
- Tell Jamie what food you like.
- Explain how to get from the station to your apartment.

points.label: Says how the writer feels about the visit
Tells Jamie what food the writer likes
Explains how to get from the station to the apartment

tasks.instruction: Pick either of the two tasks and write about it.

choices.title: Article
choices.prompt:
You see this announcement in an English-language magazine.

ARTICLES WANTED: My favorite place to relax
Where do you go to relax? What do you do there? Why is it special for you?

Write your article in about 100 words.

points.label: Says where the writer goes to relax
Says what the writer does there
Explains why the place is special

choices.title: Story
choices.prompt:
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence:

When Maria opened the door, she could not believe what she saw.

Write your story in about 100 words.

points.label: Describes what Maria saw behind the door
Tells what Maria did or felt next
